title: Brave Search API Pricing: Plans, Limits, Cost (2026)
summary: Brave Search API pricing varies based on query volume and plan type. Calculate your actual costs rather than relying on advertised base rates.
body_markdown:
## Know hidden Brave Search API costs and limits


Past the sticker price there are other meters, and they run on limits and habits you may not have priced yet.


You can be well under the quota and still get refused because two requests landed in the same second. The free plan caps you at one query per second, and that's a separate limit from your monthly quota.


### Retries and agent loops that multiply queries


Rarely does one user question mean one search.


**33.8 search calls per task** is what a web research agent makes, so one question there costs about 34 of your queries. Deep research makes 24, Google AI Mode 9.06, and ChatGPT 2.17.


**Multiply your expected tasks by the high end, not the low one, and add retries on top.**


At 34 queries a task, you will want a counter in front of every call, and a closed tool only gives you the one it shipped with. If the connector or step you need is missing, you wait on the vendor's roadmap.


Activepieces lets you generate the missing integration with AI and add it privately to your own instance, with no release to wait for.


Roughly 60% of its 746 integrations were contributed by the community, meaning most integrations are maintained by volunteers, and the count comes straight from the[community pieces folder of its open-source monorepo](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/tree/main/packages/pieces/community) , where the core sits under an MIT licence.


### The model bill on top of search


If a language model reads the results and writes the answer, you pay for its output tokens too (a token is roughly three-quarters of a word).


The chart shows the[ThinkHard price list](https://thinkhard.si/prices/) per million output tokens. Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra cost $50 each, so a long answer from either can cost more than the searches behind it.


At $20 sit Claude Opus 5.5 and, in ThinkHard's listing, the older GPT-5.6 Sol, and at $10 Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol, which means you must pay $20 to access Opus 5.5. Picking the cheaper tier cuts that line fivefold.


Whether you may store results, for how long, and whether you must credit Brave on screen is governed by Brave's terms. I can't give you the exact limits here, so read them before building a cache.


### Know which Brave Search API endpoints bill separately


Not everything sits under the web search price. The Answers feature, which has Brave generate the reply, bills tokens on top of the query. Check each endpoint you plan to call, because a feature you add later can arrive with its own meter.


What happens when you hit the quota isn't something I could confirm in Brave's documentation. It might block requests, or it might bill overage. Test it in a sandbox, or ask Brave, before launch.
